rationale: Three blocking findings: (1) negative spend from API not guarded, renders as negative currency in SpendingCard doughnut and table rows; (2) NaN/Infinity not guarded, render as literal $NaN/$Infinity strings in SpendingProgressBar label; (3) label text lacks truncate class, overflow risk at high spend values. All input validation gaps introduced by spend-display feature. All 16 acceptance criteria pass.

No injection risks; spend values safely formatted through formatSpend utility

findings.title: Negative spend not guarded; renders as negative currency
findings.problem: currentSpendValue useMemo accepts any number without validating >= 0 (line 109-110: if (typeof rawSpend === 'number')). Negative values pass to formatCurrency, rendering as $-5.50. Same issue at line 252 for table rows passed to SpendingProgressBar.
findings.impact: Negative spend displays as negative currency in doughnut and table, contradicting spending-tracking intent. Confuses users about actual spending state.
findings.recommendation: Add guard to accept only non-negative values: if (typeof rawSpend === 'number' && rawSpend >= 0) { return rawSpend }. Apply same guard at line 252 for table row spend extraction.

findings.title: NaN/Infinity not guarded; render as literal strings
findings.problem: SpendingProgressBar line 51 passes spend to formatSpend without validating Number.isFinite(). formatCurrency renders NaN/Infinity literally: $NaN or $Infinity in label.
findings.impact: Label displays broken/unintelligible text. Silent data corruption from API reaches the UI undetected, making the component unusable with invalid data.
findings.recommendation: Add validation before formatSpend: check both typeof spend === 'number' && Number.isFinite(spend) && spend >= 0, or let formatSpend handle null; invalid values should render as dash.

findings.title: Label text lacks truncate class; overflow risk
findings.problem: Span element (line 65) has whitespace-nowrap but no truncate class. Long labels (e.g., $9,999,999.99 (100%)) exceed container width and overflow without being clipped.
findings.impact: At high spend values or narrow viewports, label text breaks layout horizontally, degrading responsive design.
findings.recommendation: Add truncate class to span className: 'text-sm font-semibold leading-none whitespace-nowrap truncate text-right' to clip overflow text.
